blocks.prompt: 2. A dataset is modeled by the polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + 5x - 2\). Find whether the point \(x = 2\) lies on the curve.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh asal mein Factor Theorem ka sawal hai, bas lafz kahani wale hain. Is exercise mein "point \(x = 2\) curve par hai" ka matlab hai ke model wahan zero deta hai, yani \(P(2) = 0\); graph wahan \(x\)-axis ko chhoota hai.
Find kya karna hai? Haan ya na: \(x = 2\) curve par hai ya nahi.
Plan: \(P(2)\) nikalein; zero aaye to jawab haan, aur \(x - 2\) factor hai; aakhir mein synthetic division se tasdeeq.
Yaad rakhein: is exercise mein "curve par hona", "response zero hona", "error-free hona" aur "factor hona", sab ka matlab ek hi hai: value zero aani chahiye.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(P(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + 5x - 2\) aur point \(x = 2\).
Humein find karna hai: kya \(x = 2\) curve par hai, yani kya \(P(2) = 0\)?
Tareeqa: Factor Theorem kehta hai: \(x - a\) tab hi factor hai jab \(P(a) = 0\) ho. Yahan \(a = 2\), is liye sirf ek value \(P(2)\) nikalni hai. Lambi division ki zaroorat nahi.
Book ki Example 10 bhi isi tarah ek value nikal kar faisla karti hai.

\(P(2)\) nikalein
\[P(2) = 2^3 - 4(2)^2 + 5(2) - 2\]
\[= 8 - 4(4) + 10 - 2\]
\[= 8 - 16 + 10 - 2\]
\[= 0\]
Kyun: \(x = 2\) rakhne se woh remainder milta hai jo \(x - 2\) se divide karne par aata (Remainder Theorem). Pehle powers: \(2^3 = 8\), \(2^2 = 4\). Phir multiply: \(4 \times 4 = 16\), \(5 \times 2 = 10\). Phir baen se daen jama aur minus: \(8 - 16 = -8\), \(-8 + 10 = 2\), \(2 - 2 = 0\).
Dhyan dein: \(-4(2)^2\) mein minus sign 4 ke saath hai; \(2^2 = 4\) pehle karein, phir \(-4 \times 4 = -16\).

Natija nikalein
\[P(2) = 0\]
\[\Rightarrow (x - 2) \text{ is a factor}\]
Kyun: Value zero ka matlab remainder zero. Factor Theorem ke mutabiq \(x - 2\) poora poora divide karta hai, aur \(x = 2\) is polynomial ka root hai. Is liye point \(x = 2\) curve par hai (\(x\)-axis wali jagah par).

Synthetic division se tasdeeq (\(x - 2\) se)
Coefficients \(1,\ -4,\ 5,\ -2\) aur \(a = 2\):
1 neeche utarein; \(1 \times 2 = 2\), \(-4 + 2 = -2\);
\(-2 \times 2 = -4\), \(5 - 4 = 1\);
\(1 \times 2 = 2\), \(-2 + 2 = 0\).
\[\text{Quotient} = x^2 - 2x + 1\]
\[\text{Remainder} = 0 \;\checkmark\]
\[P(x) = (x - 2)(x - 1)^2\]
Kyun: Section 9.1.3 wali synthetic division bhi wahi remainder 0 deti hai, to jawab pakka hua. Bonus: quotient \(x^2 - 2x + 1 = (x - 1)^2\) hai, yani poori factorization bhi mil gayi.
Khud sochiye: kya \(x = 1\) bhi is curve par hai? (\(P(1) = 1 - 4 + 5 - 2 = 0\), haan.)
Natija yaad rakhne ka asaan tareeqa: value zero to factor, value non-zero to factor nahi. Yeh ek line poori exercise ki chaabi hai.
blocks.final_answer: Haan. \(P(2) = 0\), is liye \(x = 2\) curve par hai (aur \(x - 2\) factor hai: \(P(x) = (x - 2)(x - 1)^2\)).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key (PDF 307) mein is sawal ka jawab number 3 par chhapa hai: "\(x = 2\) lies on the curve", jo hamare hal se milta hai. Key ka number 2 ("\(x = -1\) is a valid point") is sawal ka nahi hai; key mein 10 jawab hain jabke sawal sirf 7 chhape hain.
